clue.text: Severe criticism, but mostly getting on

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: save can mean but or except, as in 'all save one'

explanation.surface: A critic delivers a harsh verdict while mostly getting along with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' looks like a mere connective, yet it is SAVE in the sense of 'except', trimmed to SAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A savaging is a fierce verbal attack, the noun for tearing a work or person to pieces in a review.

clue.text: Meagre item, without an end

indicators.note: lacking an end means the final letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: a thing is an item or object

explanation.surface: A paltry object is described as having no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and meagre are synonyms for something scanty or sparse in quantity.

clue.text: Exist to bring in hi-tech design in area of gaming

indicators.note: bringing something in places it inside the other word

blocks.note: to exist is to be; 'are' is a form of that verb

explanation.surface: Computer design techniques are brought into the games industry.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall full of coin-operated video and slot machines, a place for playing games.

clue.text: Trawling item? Heartless shore, ultimate damage

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: A fishing net is wrecked on a shore, the final blow.
explanation.walkthrough: COAST loses its middle A. 'Damage' is colloquial for cost, as in 'what's the damage?'
explanation.definitionFit: Net cost is the final amount paid after deductions; damage is informal slang for a bill or price.

clue.text: Girl pursuing crimes heading off to travel in winter

indicators.note: losing the heading means the first letter of the word is removed
pursuing means coming after, so the girl's name is placed second

blocks.note: vices are wicked practices or crimes

explanation.surface: A young woman chases after criminals as winter travel sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice-skate is to glide across frozen water on blades, a way of getting about in cold weather.

clue.text: Lewd line, improper rub, depraved (but not very)

indicators.note: something improper is not in its proper order, so the letters are rearranged
not very tells us to drop the abbreviation for very from the word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A list of shocking descriptions of a crude rub, depraved but only mildly so.
explanation.walkthrough: VICIOUS loses V, the abbreviation for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricious means lecherous or salacious, a literary synonym for lewd.

clue.text: Add fizz to region, picking up sources of true enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up suggests lifting, so the word is read from bottom to top
sources are where things begin, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Bringing sparkle to a district by gathering real enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate a drink is to charge it with gas, which makes it bubbly and fizzy.

clue.text: Declining to accept overtures of Auber, Rossini and Haydn - something too often played

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it inside, so the other letters go within
an overture opens a piece, so the opening letters of the composers are taken

blocks.note: a declining condition is getting worse

explanation.surface: An orchestra tires of opera overtures by three composers, one hackneyed concert piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtures' fits the musical scene literally, which hides its job of taking only the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhorse is a hackneyed, overfamiliar musical or theatrical piece that gets performed again and again.

clue.text: Poorly-formed note from religious scholar

blocks.note: n. is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A badly written memo arrives from a theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a musical letter A to G, but here it is n., the footnote abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Cruden compiled the famous eighteenth-century concordance to the Bible, a landmark of scriptural study.

clue.text: Get close, but start to move back

indicators.note: the starting letter is told to move to the back, rotating the word

explanation.surface: Approaching something, only to begin retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to get or obtain it in return for work.

clue.text: A bit of countryside crossed with a twisting minor route

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just a small part, here its opening letter
twisting distorts the letters so they come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rural patch is crossed by a winding back lane.
explanation.definitionFit: An access road is a small side road giving entry to a property or site rather than a through route.

clue.text: Weapon with extra force producing stir

indicators.note: having something extra means an additional letter is slipped in

blocks.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A gun given more power causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To riffle is to ruffle or disturb lightly, as wind ripples water or fingers flick through pages.

clue.text: Personal history: renown curtailed, entirely ruined, name lost

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter goes
something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt
lost means the letter for name is taken out before rebuilding

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A biography in which a reputation is cut down, wholly wrecked, and the name forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: FAME loses its E; ENTIRELY loses its N and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree charts one's ancestry, a record of the lineage behind an individual.

clue.text: Hunter almost ready: man with weapon follows

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped
follows places the armed man after the first part

blocks.note: set means ready, as in 'ready, set, go'
an archer is armed with a bow

explanation.surface: A hunter is nearly prepared, with an armed companion behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is someone who seeks or looks for something, as a hunter seeks quarry.

clue.text: Dance publication backed return of fling

indicators.note: backed means run backwards, so the word is read right to left
returning means going back, so this word is also read in reverse

blocks.note: to lob is to throw or fling

explanation.surface: A magazine supported a revival of a fling, perhaps a romantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip or frolic playfully, a lively leaping that is close to dancing.

clue.text: Admit daughter consumes cereal from a particular store

blocks.note: to own up is to admit
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl's breakfast cereal, conceded to come from one shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' only joins the pieces here; the cereal simply sits before the daughter rather than inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: Own-brand goods are made for and sold under the name of a specific retailer, so they come only from its shops.

clue.text: Change official order after intervention by Queen

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the royal letter sits inside the order

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
OM is the Order of Merit
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A government decree is altered once the monarch steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official order' reads as one phrase, a decree, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to change or improve it, especially an institution or law.

clue.text: Thatcher, perhaps, to damage rooftop room, dropping one reed, initially

indicators.note: dropping a letter means it falls out of the word

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a garret is an attic room
first letter of reed; only one of the two in the room goes

explanation.surface: A roof thatcher damages an attic by losing a reed, fitting since thatch is made of reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the UK prime minister; 'perhaps' marks her first name as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is the given name of the former British prime minister, so Thatcher is one bearer of it.

clue.text: Flowering plant: it's able to run wild

indicators.note: running wild means behaving without order, so the letters scatter into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A garden plant is capable of spreading uncontrolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a perennial garden plant bearing feathery plumes of small blooms.

clue.text: Line in unconventional small pets

indicators.note: in places the line inside the word for unconventional

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A row of quirky little animals kept at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' reads as animals, but it means favoured people, terms of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlings are beloved people, and pets is a fond term for favourites, as in teacher's pet.

clue.text: A late party: night's beginning, stir yourself

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter only

blocks.note: a wake is a gathering held for someone late, that is dead

explanation.surface: Someone urged to rouse themselves for a party that runs late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests a time of night, but it means deceased; a wake is a gathering after a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To awaken is to rouse oneself from sleep, which is what stirring yourself means.

clue.text: Stone in trap showing effect of reflected light

indicators.note: in places the weight unit inside the word for a trap

blocks.note: a lure is a bait or trap
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A gemstone caught in a snare glints in the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the soft sheen or gleam of a surface that bounces light back.

clue.text: Oaf uncovered tummy when tucking into smoked salmon

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle
tucking into puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: lox is cured salmon, an American Jewish deli word

explanation.surface: A clumsy lout bares his belly while wolfing down smoked salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is a clumsy, stupid person, an informal word for a lumbering fool.

clue.text: I must turn a failing flowering plant

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters collapse and are rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A gardener resolves to tend a wilting plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasturtium is a trailing garden annual with bright orange or yellow blooms and edible leaves.

clue.text: One who steers round a cable

indicators.note: going round something encloses it

blocks.note: a cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A helmsman guides a boat around a mooring rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like a ship's rope, but it is coaxial cable, as used for TV aerials.
explanation.definitionFit: Coax is the short form of coaxial cable, the shielded wire that carries television signals.

clue.text: Diffident accepting Special in snug

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A shy person takes a special offer while tucked up comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and snug both describe somewhere warm, comfortable and sheltered.

clue.text: Article, say, to intend dismissing source of sea

indicators.note: dismissing the source sends away the starting letter of the word

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: A piece of writing aims to drop the origin of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: Book is about hospital activities - that is, diagnostic interventions

indicators.note: about means around, so the word wraps the following letters

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
i.e. is Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A book discusses hospital procedures used to diagnose illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' wraps both the hospital piece and 'that is' together, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopsy removes a tissue sample for laboratory examination, a procedure used to identify disease.
